candidates.title: Log mobile game test sessions

demandEvidence.chore: Record mobile game battery, temperature, frame drops and session notes, then move exported logs into a Google Sheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Right now I type it into a notes app during the session, then later export a CSV from that app and paste it into a Google Sheet.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable CSV row for each supplied game test log, with duplicate files flagged before entry.
inputs: Synthetic test row with date, device label, battery, temperature, frame drops and session note
Operator supplied CSV export from the notes app
Synthetic file name and upload timestamp
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test run after supplying a completed CSV export; no phone or Drive trigger is assumed.
steps: Read the supplied CSV rows and check the expected columns.
Normalize dates and device labels into a proposed row format.
Compare row content and file name against prior test inputs to flag likely duplicates.
Prepare a Google Sheets ready CSV and a short list of rejected rows.
Ask a person to review the rows and import the approved file.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: With a small synthetic CSV containing valid, malformed and repeated rows, confirm that valid values are preserved and repeated rows are flagged for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester supplies and checks the test records, confirms duplicate flags, and imports approved rows; no live phone, Drive or Google Sheets connection is proposed.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports CSV parsing, deduplication, file triggers or Sheets writes.
Actual log fields, file formats and reliable duplicate keys are unknown.
The post describes one tester; a recurring paying customer group is only a hypothesis.

ease.reason: A beginner can test proposed row checks with synthetic logs, but no supplied reference supports the workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: game QA contractors may pay for tidier session logs; the post shows no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week CSV mock is bounded; actual formats and duplicate rules remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed import-preparation loop repeats, but no automation support is supplied and a tester must review and import.

evidence.reason: The retained context describes log fields and a notes-to-CSV-to-Sheets chore; frequency beyond the stated habit and wider demand are unknown.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the retained context supports a concrete logging chore, but implementation support and evidence of a paying customer are absent.

candidates.title: Plan recovery for failed agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Developers write checkpointers and recovery logic and handle idempotency for agent runs.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A human reviewed recovery checklist draft for one supplied failed agent run.
inputs: Synthetic run log with failed step and timestamp
Operator supplied description of expected task result
Operator supplied list of safe retry limits
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a review after a synthetic or authorized test agent run reports a failure.
steps: Read the supplied failure summary and expected result.
Group the issue as retry, checkpoint or duplicate-action risk using operator supplied rules.
Draft a bounded recovery checklist with the evidence for each suggested step.
Flag missing state or uncertain actions instead of proposing an automatic retry.
Have an operator verify the checklist before changing or rerunning any agent.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic logs with a transient error, missing checkpoint and possible duplicate action, verify that each checklist cites an input and flags uncertain or irreversible actions for human review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer supplies logs and retry rules, reviews every suggestion, and authorizes any code change or rerun; no agent execution or recovery integration is proposed.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports log ingestion, checkpointing, idempotency or agent recovery.
The source does not specify agent types, failure classes or safe retry rules.
No repeat frequency or buyer willingness to pay is established.

ease.reason: A beginner can draft a checklist from synthetic logs, but no supplied reference supports recovery mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agents may pay for recovery support; this comment does not show buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A checklist mock is bounded, but agent types, retry rules and safe recovery behavior are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed output is a human reviewed checklist; no automated execution or recovery capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The comment names checkpointers, recovery logic and idempotency, but gives no example, recurrence or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the comment identifies agent recovery work, but the exact workflow is underspecified and no implementation evidence is supplied.
